record.original_question: For any positive integer initial value a_0, define a sequence by a_{n+1}=a_n/2 when a_n is even and a_{n+1}=3a_n+1 when a_n is odd. Must the sequence eventually reach the value 1 for every positive integer a_0?

evidence.quote: The Collatz conjecture states that for every positive integer a_0, the sequence obtained by taking a_{n+1}=a_n/2 if a_n is even and a_{n+1}=3a_n+1 if a_n is odd eventually attains the value 1.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a positive integer $a_0$, define a sequence $(a_n)_{n\ge 0}$ of positive integers recursively by
\[
a_{n+1} = \begin{cases} a_n/2 & \text{if } a_n \text{ is even,} \\ 3a_n + 1 & \text{if } a_n \text{ is odd.} \end{cases}
\]
Prove or disprove: for every positive integer $a_0$, there exists a nonnegative integer $n$ such that $a_n = 1$.
artifact.status_search_result: The Collatz (3n+1) conjecture is a famous long-standing open problem. The strongest known partial result is due to Terence Tao (2019/2022), showing that almost all Collatz orbits attain almost bounded values, but the full conjecture remains unresolved. Numerical verification has been extended beyond 2^68 by Barina and others.

status_evidence.title: Almost all orbits of the Collatz map attain almost bounded values
status_evidence.snippet: We show that for any function f tending to infinity, the Collatz orbit of almost every positive integer attains a value less than f(n).
status_evidence.claim: Best known partial result; full Collatz conjecture remains open.

status_evidence.title: Convergence verification of the Collatz problem
status_evidence.snippet: Verification of the Collatz conjecture up to 2^68.
status_evidence.claim: Numerical verification extends to large bounds, but no proof exists.
